back: The purpose for which land is used: crops, livestock, forestry, wildlife, aquaculture, settlement or protection.
Farming fish and other water organisms in ponds, tanks, dams or cages.
Land set aside by law to conserve wildlife, plants, scenery or water catchments, e.g. a national park.
Steep slopes erode and cannot be mechanised; valley bottoms waterlog; high altitude brings cold and frost.
Low or unreliable rain, very high or low temperatures, frost and strong wind restrict which crops and animals can be kept.
Shallow, stony, infertile, acidic, salty or badly drained soils limit cropping.

front: Which insect has limited cattle keeping in some hot, low-lying valleys?
back: The tsetse fly, which spreads trypanosomiasis.
Too many people or animals depending on too little land, so it is overused and degraded.
Fragmentation, shorter fallows, cultivation of slopes and wetlands, overgrazing, deforestation and erosion.
